title: Indefinite waitings in MIRELA systems
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; two-example model-checking feasibility result
evidence_note: Translation to PRISM classifies deadlock, starvation and unbounded waiting. Demonstrated on two examples; one starvation result disappears after timing changes. Runtime depends on carefully chosen constants with a large gcd; stochastic and more complex structures remain future work.

title: Verification of railway interlocking systems
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; bounded real-station case study
evidence_note: One station model has 14 routes, 7 points and 7 track circuits; 132 invariants and 7 CTL properties detect injected data errors. The paper reports 10 hours versus 100 hours for writing seven CTL formulas in its route-growth experiment. One relatively small interlocking; only safety properties, with liveness and larger interacting models left open.

title: Automatic Generation of Minimal Cut Sets
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; one aircraft hydraulic model comparison
sections_checked: runtime table and prior-work comparison caveat
evidence_note: For the reported A320 hydraulic model, systematic generation takes 13 minutes versus 65 minutes for the naive strategy and returns the same cut sets. Fault modes are supplied/identified by the analyst; comparison with prior SAL results is explicitly not controlled. Do not generalize the fivefold result beyond this case.

title: Breaking Dense Structures: Proving Stability of Densely Structured Hybrid Systems
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; large gains on selected dense models with unchanged counterexample
evidence_note: Graph relaxation cuts decomposition effort from 13h22m to 0.05s on complete K5 and from 1h46m to 0.06s on Spidercam; cruise-controller runtime stays 0.060s. Relaxation introduces conservative/spurious trajectories and can require stepwise reconstruction, making benefit model-structure-dependent.

title: Formal Verification of Real-Time Function Blocks Using PVS
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; two industrial case studies
evidence_note: Two nuclear-industry function-block case studies use PVS formalization; the analysis exposes an initialization failure and a missing implementation assumption. Concrete defect/assumption findings, but no controlled cross-project defect-rate, cost, or certification-time comparison.

title: Using Indexed and Synchronous Events to Model and Validate Cyber-Physical Systems
review_status: citation-follow-up full-text audit complete; language/tool demonstrations on two case studies
sections_checked: indexed and synchronous event language extensions
evidence_note: TTM extensions are demonstrated on train-control and nuclear shutdown models. In the nuclear example, idealized instantaneous synchronization is refined by separating plant/controller actions and checking a bounded response-time property. Demonstrates modeling expressiveness, not deployed failure reduction or industrial-scale performance.
